_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process: exponential hazards 0.12 (treated) and 0.20 (control), tau = 4; RMST = (1 - exp(-h tau)) / h

agreement.claim: both engines report the same RMST, standard error and difference in each arm
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: 0 at ten significant digits on every key, including the standard errors: Python's written-out Greenwood-type variance reproduces R's se(rmean) exactly. harness/survival_examples.test.py checks both against a Kaplan-Meier computed from scratch, and records that lifelines' return_variance, used as an SE, would be 1.24 years.

recovery.claim: each arm's RMST and the difference are close to the fixture's

calibration.rule: about 1.3 times the measured 99th percentile miss, rounded up
calibration.limits: At 300 per arm the difference's miss (0.32) was close to the effect (0.42); the fixture uses 700 per arm.
